note: Annual tune up on the beckett. Changed the nozzle, .75 80A, new oil filter, cleaned the electrodes and the cad cell eye. Smoke zero, CO 12 ppm, draft minus .02. Running good.
no heat call. circulator was seized, swapped it with a taco 007. bled the air out, pressure back to 12 psi. upstairs zone heating now

Not cooling. Run capacitor was bulging, replaced with a 45/5 MFD dual run cap. Condenser fan and compressor both running, temp split 19 degrees. Told the customer the coil is dirty, should get it cleaned in the spring.
Cleaned both heads, washed the filters, foamed the coils and flushed the drain lines. No parts.
Furnace short cycling. Flame sensor was coated, cleaned it with emery cloth instead of replacing. Changed the 16x25x1 filter. Ran it through 3 cycles, all good.
tune up. didnt change the filter, customer had one on the shelf and wants to do it himself. replaced nozzle 1.00 60B. co was 8 ppm. recommend replacing the flue pipe next year its getting rusty
Outdoor unit iced up solid. Defrost board bad, replaced it. Did a manual defrost, checked it cycles out ok. Suction 118 psi, superheat 10.
No hot water. Pilot wouldn't stay lit, replaced the thermocouple. Lit it and it held. Flushed a bit of sediment while I was there.
Installed new 3 zone Mitsubishi MXZ-3C24NA outdoor unit on a wall bracket. Ran 3 line sets, pulled vacuum to 400 microns, held for 15 minutes. Released the charge.
Inspection only for the estimate. Boiler is a 2003 Weil-McLain, heat exchanger has some cracking near the back section. Didnt do any work. Need to send them a replacement quote.
Uh so this was the annual. Replaced the nozzle and the pump strainer, filter too. Combustion test, efficiency 84 percent, smoke trace. That's it.
Spring start up. Cleaned condenser coil, checked charge, all good. Cap reading 43 on a 45 rated, still within spec so left it. Cleared the condensate line.
Inducer motor making a racket, bearings shot. Replaced inducer. Customer also asked about a humidifier, said I'd get back to her with a price.
water dripping from the bedroom head. drain line clogged, blew it out with nitrogen. no parts
Annual service. Cleaned the heat exchanger, new gaskets on the cleanout covers. Checked the relief valve and the low water cutoff. Pressure 15 psi, temp 180.
Tune up. Washed outdoor coil, checked reversing valve switches over fine. Filter is the customers, they change it. Static pressure 0.5 in wc.
No heat. Ignitor was cracked. Put in a new Beckett ignitor. While I was at it changed the nozzle. Should come back and do the full tune up in a couple weeks.
Flushed tank, checked anode rod, its about half gone but ok for now. Tested the T&P valve.

expected._relabel: Anode rod "about half gone but ok for now": flagging it for a later visit is a reasonable call too. Relabeled after the first AI run; see docs/AI-EVALUATION.md.

note: Contactor pitted and chattering. Swapped in a new 30 amp single pole contactor. Unit running. Suction 70 psi head 250.
Error code on the outdoor unit, fan motor not spinning. Ordered a fan motor, put the old one back together for now, its running but noisy. Coming back when the part comes in.
Fall tune up. New filter, cleaned burners, checked flame sensor reading 4.2 microamps. Gas pressure 3.5 in wc on the manifold. CO in the flue 22 ppm.
Low pressure again, auto fill valve wasn't feeding. Replaced the fill valve and set it to 12. Expansion tank seems ok but keep an eye on it.
Annual done. nozzle filter strainer. CO 10. all set.
Installed new Fujitsu heat pump, AOU24RLXFZH outdoor with the matching air handler. New pad and a disconnect. Vacuum to 350 microns. Walked the customer through the thermostat.
Customer complained about high bills. Checked everything, charge is fine, coil clean. Their ductwork in the attic is leaking bad though. Gave them a number for an insulation guy. Nothing replaced.
Head in the office not cooling. Found it on dry mode lol. Set it back to cool, cleaned the filters while I was there. Remote batteries were dead too, put new ones in.
Pressure switch failing to close. Cleared the clogged condensate trap, switch closes now. Didnt need the new pressure switch I brought.
Tune up on the Navien. Cleaned the burner and the condensate trap, checked the neutralizer, its spent, replaced the media. Flue gas CO 35 ppm, CO2 9.1 percent.

Oil smell in the basement. Fitting on the oil line at the filter was weeping. Tightened it and put a new flare fitting on. Cleaned up the spill. Tank is old, customer should think about replacing it soon.
Installed new Bradford White 40 gallon, RE340S6. New expansion tank, new gas flex and shut off. Tested for leaks, lit it up.
Spring service. Cleaned outdoor coil. Low on charge, found a leak at the flare on the line set, re-flared it and added 8 oz of R410A. Superheat 9 after.
Blower motor capacitor bad, 7.5 MFD. Replaced it, blower running at full speed. Told them filter needs changing but they want to buy their own.
Startup on new system done. Charged to 10 degrees subcool. Temp split 20. Need to come back and seal the line set penetration, didn't have the foam with me.
Emergency heat call. Heat strips not coming on, sequencer burnt. Replaced sequencer. Strips working, house warming up.
Checked it over before the season, everything looks good, customer only wanted a safety check, no tune up this year. No parts. CO 15.
Zone valve on the kitchen zone stuck closed. Replaced the powerhead, not the whole valve. Zone opens and heats now. Other two zone valves are original, might go soon.
